utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-02-61-PT, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Deronjic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I have the parties for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon representing the Office of the Prosecutor in these proceedings. Appearing with me is Mr. David Leese.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Slobodan Cvijetic, lead counsel for the accused Miroslav Deronjic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The accused, I would like to find out whether you can hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I can hear very well, and I understand everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a Status Conference to look at the preparatory stages for this case before the trial is held. The first point, I wanted to find out from the Defence counsel is about his assignment to this case, because the previous record showed that the assignment was for a limited period. May I know whether you are now taking the case forward?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I shall be appearing for the accused Miroslav Deronjic throughout the trial, and on his behalf, I have submitted to the Court all the documents necessary for him to be assigned counsel throughout the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'll turn to the Prosecution on the delivery of supporting material. How far has the Prosecution gone in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution has provided to Mr. Deronjic all of the confirming materials in a language he understands. We did so on the day of his initial appearance. We have subsequently provided to him all prior statements that he has made pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) and we have additional discovery materials that we will be providing to him later this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The additional material you are talking about, is this still under 66(A)(i) or is it under 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's under 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Any disclosures under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I believe there will be some materials under Rule 68 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. When you say this week, because this is Wednesday today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I am advised by my staff that these materials currently have been copied and they are available to be disclosed. It's just a question of finalising the package of materials to provide to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. The Trial Chamber is keen to have this stage of the preparatory stage completed as quickly as possible, because it normally holds the preparation stages because the Defence are not given the materials on time. I know that the form of the indictment decision has just been released by the Trial Chamber, but the amendments which are being sought or which are ordered under the motion by the Defence have nothing to do with variation of the charges. They are dealing with details of the factual allegations and forms of liability. So the disclosure process should be able to go on on time and as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any comments from the Defence on the process of disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have already had our first meeting with Mr. Harmon, and we have received some promises from him that the disclosure will proceed according to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to say that so far there hasn't been a meeting by the Senior Legal Officer according to the Rules on the preparation of this case, but the meeting will be scheduled soon thereafter. So the Trial Chamber would very much appreciate the process of disclosure to move very fast, because then it will provide materials for discussion at the meeting which the Defence may want to deal with. Looking at this case and the main stages that are remaining, the Trial Chamber is of the view that it should be -- the trial -- the preparatory stage should be completed by the end of February 2003 because it's a fairly short case, and all things being equal, there should be no hitches in the preparatory stage. I would now turn to the accused. I would like to find out if there is anything he would like to raise regarding his stay at the Detention Unit. Anything to do with your health or any other matters that you'd like Trial Chamber is of the view that it should be -- the trial -- the preparatory stage should be completed by the end of February 2003 because it's a fairly short case, and all things being equal, there should be no hitches in the preparatory stage. I would now turn to the accused. I would like to find out whether there is anything he would like to raise regarding his stay at the Detention Unit. Anything to do with your health or any other matters that you'd like the Trial Chamber to know about. And if everything is okay at the Detention Unit, then that's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point in time, I have nothing special to say. Within the Rules that we have been accorded, I am quite satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. I would like to find out from the Defence, there was an application for leave to file a motion confidentially, and leave was granted by the Trial Chamber, and it's been some time. So I wanted to find out whether there will be any follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I thought it would not be fair to file this motion before I talk to Mr. Harmon or, rather, to the Office of the Prosecutor. We have had this discussion, and now my client and I can finally reach a decision as to whether we are going to file this motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Any other matters from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other matters the Defence would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, not for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. The senior legal officer will schedule a meeting as I have said as soon as he is ready by intimation from both parties, and thereafter a time schedule will be issued for the preparatory stage to be completed in this case so that the trial can perhaps take place early next year. Very well. There being no other business, this is the end of the Status Conference and the Court will rise.
